title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text: R/bib.R

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text: cz_update_bib

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Description
Scans Quarto / R Markdown documents for @key citations, looks the keys up among the pinned citekeys in your Zotero library, and writes a bibliography file containing only the cited items. Zotero is the source of truth for the content of each reference; the documents decide which references are needed.

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Usage
cz_update_bib(
  qmd = NULL,
  out = NULL,
  format = NULL,
  bare = NULL,
  allow_incomplete = FALSE,
  auth = cz_auth(),
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE),
  quiet = FALSE
)

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




qmd
Documents to scan for @key citations. Defaults to every .qmd and .Rmd file under the working directory, skipping hidden and underscore-prefixed directories, renv, packrat and node_modules.


out
Bibliography file to write. Defaults to the file named by bibliography: in the documents’ YAML front matter (or the project’s _quarto.yml), else references.bib. If the documents name different files, out must be given.


format
"bib" or "yaml"; inferred from out if NULL.


bare
Optional files (e.g. CSVs) scanned for bare citekey-shaped tokens such as Ebihara2006. Missing ones only warn.


allow_incomplete
Write the file even if keys cited in qmd are not found in Zotero.


auth
Credentials from cz_auth().


cache
Passed to cz_fetch_items(): keep a local copy of the library so repeat runs are fast. Defaults to getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE).


quiet
Suppress the summary message.

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Details
Safety: if a key cited in a document is not found in Zotero, the function stops and leaves the existing output file untouched (a bibliography that silently loses entries breaks the render). Set allow_incomplete = TRUE to write what was found anyway. Keys found only in bare files, and duplicate citekeys in Zotero (the first match is used), give warnings. The file is only rewritten when its content would change, so unchanged bibliographies keep their modification time.

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Output formats
"bib" (default) writes BibLaTeX using Zotero’s own exporter, with each entry keyed by its pinned citekey; it works with every Quarto output format, including Typst. "yaml" writes CSL-YAML (a references: list with id and citation-key set to the citekey). The format is inferred from the extension of out (.bib or .yaml/.yml).

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Value
out, invisibly (handy for targets::tar_target(format = "file")).

title: Write a bibliography file from the references cited in your documents
text:
Examples
# reads ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID / ZOTERO_API_KEY from the environment
cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd")
cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd", out = "references.yaml")

title: Extract pandoc citation keys used in a qmd/Rmd file
text: cz_qmd_keys

title: Extract pandoc citation keys used in a qmd/Rmd file
text:
Description
Strips fenced code blocks first (so @ in R code is never mistaken for a citation), finds @key tokens, then drops Quarto cross-references (?@fig-x, ?@tbl-x, ?@eq-x, …), which use the same syntax but are not bibliography citations.

title: Extract pandoc citation keys used in a qmd/Rmd file
text:
Usage
cz_qmd_keys(
  path,
  crossref_prefixes = c("fig", "tbl", "eq", "sec", "lst", "thm", "lem", "cor", "prp",
    "cnj", "def", "exm", "exr", "rem", "sol", "nte")
)

title: Extract pandoc citation keys used in a qmd/Rmd file
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




path
Path to a .qmd or .Rmd file.


crossref_prefixes
Cross-reference prefixes to drop (without the trailing hyphen).

title: Extract pandoc citation keys used in a qmd/Rmd file
text:
Value
Sorted character vector of unique citation keys (no leading @).

title: Extract pandoc citation keys used in a qmd/Rmd file
text:
Examples

qmd <- tempfile(fileext = ".qmd")
writeLines(c(
  "Species evolve by natural selection [@Darwin1859]; see @fig-map.",
  "```{r}",
  "x@slot  # not a citation",
  "```"
), qmd)
cz_qmd_keys(qmd)

[1] "Darwin1859"

title: Which key formula citezot will use
text:
Description
In order: getOption("citezot.key_format"); the Better BibTeX pattern in your Zotero profile (see Details); Better BibTeX’s default pattern.

title: Which key formula citezot will use
text:
Usage
cz_key_format()

title: Which key formula citezot will use
text:
Details
Detection of the Zotero profile reads one line of its prefs.js and only happens when a key is generated, never at load. Set options(citezot.key_format = ...) to choose a formula yourself and skip the detection, and options(citezot.zotero_profile = "<folder>") if Zotero keeps its profile somewhere unusual. The source in use is reported once per session.

title: Which key formula citezot will use
text:
Value
A list with formula and source ("option", "zotero profile" or "default").

title: Which key formula citezot will use
text:
Examples

options(citezot.key_format = "auth.lower + year")
cz_key_format()

$formula
[1] "auth.lower + year"

$source
[1] "option"

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text: R/read.R

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text: cz_fetch_items

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text:
Description
Uses the /items/top endpoint (excludes notes, attachments and other child items) and pages through the whole library using the Total-Results header. After the first page, the remaining pages are requested in parallel (at most getOption("citezot.max_active", 4) at a time, and throttled) and the library version is checked so that a library edited mid-download is re-fetched rather than returned inconsistent.

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text:
Usage
cz_fetch_items(
  auth = cz_auth(),
  page_size = 100,
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE),
  refresh = FALSE
)

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




auth
Credentials from cz_auth().


page_size
Items per request (Zotero’s maximum is 100).


cache
Use and update the local cache? Defaults to getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE).


refresh
If TRUE, ignore any existing cache and download the whole library (the cache, if enabled, is then rewritten).

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text:
Details
A full download of a large library takes a while. With cache = TRUE the items are stored in a local file (in tools::R_user_dir("citezot", "cache"), or getOption("citezot.cache_dir")), and later calls download only what changed since: one request if nothing changed, otherwise the changed items plus the lists of deleted and trashed items. The cache holds the library’s bibliographic metadata, never your API key. It is opt-in: nothing is written to disk unless you ask, either here or with options(citezot.cache = TRUE). Use refresh = TRUE to ignore the cache and download everything again, and cz_clear_cache() to delete it.

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text:
Value
A list of CSL-JSON items (plain lists, simplifyVector = FALSE). The order is not guaranteed.

title: Fetch every top-level item in a Zotero library as CSL-JSON
text:
Examples
items <- cz_fetch_items()
length(items)

# Keep a local copy, so later calls download only what changed
items <- cz_fetch_items(cache = TRUE)

title: Extract bare (no @) citekey-shaped tokens from a text/data file
text:
Description
For files that reference sources informally (e.g. a CSV “comments” column saying “defined in Dubuisson2013a”). Matches an author-shaped run of letters (hyphens allowed) immediately followed by a 19
/20
year and an optional lowercase disambiguator, e.g. Ebihara2006, Boucheron-Dubuisson2024. Deliberately conservative: Ebihara 2006 or Hsu7949 do not match.

text:
Usage
cz_bare_keys(path)

title: Extract bare (no @) citekey-shaped tokens from a text/data file
text:
Arguments



Arguments
Description




path
Path to the file to scan.

title: Extract bare (no @) citekey-shaped tokens from a text/data file
text:
Value
Sorted character vector of unique citekey-shaped tokens.

title: Extract bare (no @) citekey-shaped tokens from a text/data file
text:

notes <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("site,comment", "A,defined in Darwin1859", "B,see Ebihara 2006"), notes)
cz_bare_keys(notes) # "Ebihara 2006" does not match

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text: R/add.R

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text: cz_add

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text:
Description
Looks up the metadata for a DOI (via the public Crossref API), checks that the item is not already in your library, and creates it. The default is a dry run: the library is read and Crossref is queried, but nothing is written to Zotero. Use dry_run = FALSE to create the item.

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text:
Usage
cz_add(
  id,
  key = NULL,
  collection = NULL,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  auth = cz_auth(),
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE)
)

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




id
A DOI, with or without a https://doi.org/ or doi: prefix.


key
Optional citekey to pin on the new item, e.g. "Kent2002". It must be usable as a pandoc citation key and not already used in your library. Use "auto" to generate one from your Better BibTeX formula (see cz_suggest_key() and cz_key_format()); a letter is appended if the key is taken. The key is shown in the dry run.


collection
Optional collection to add the item to: its 8-character key, or its exact name.


dry_run
If TRUE (default), show what would be created and write nothing.


auth
Credentials from cz_auth() (a key with write access to write).


cache
Passed to cz_fetch_items(), which is used for the duplicate check.

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text:
Details
The new item is built from Zotero’s own template for its type, so it only contains fields valid for that type. The citekey, if you give one, is pinned in the same request (the native citationKey field), so there is no moment where the item exists without it. Only DOIs registered with Crossref are supported for now; ISBN, arXiv and PMID lookups are planned.
Creating is retry-safe: each request carries a random Zotero-Write-Token, so a retried request after a network hiccup cannot create the item twice. Existing items are never changed or deleted.
Crossref asks clients to identify themselves with a contact address to use its faster pool. citezot never sends an address by itself; to opt in, set options(citezot.mailto = "you@example.org").

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text:
Value
Invisibly, a list with item (the payload), key (the new Zotero item ID, or NULL), existing (matching rows of cz_find() if the item was already in the library) and written.

title: Add an item to your Zotero library from a DOI
text:
Examples
cz_add("10.3767/000651906X622210", key = "Ebihara2006")        # preview
cz_add("10.3767/000651906X622210", key = "Ebihara2006", dry_run = FALSE)

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
This guide follows one manuscript from the first citation to a rendered document. The chunks that need your Zotero account are shown but not run here; the parts that work offline are run.
library(citezot)

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
Setup
Before starting you need a Zotero API key, your user ID in ~/.Renviron, and citekeys on your items. the setup guide walks through this. Check that citezot can see your credentials (the key is never printed):

cz_auth()
#> <cz_auth> user library 1234567 (API key hidden)

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
The loop: cite, update, render
In manuscript.qmd, cite as usual and point Quarto at the file citezot will write:
---
title: "On the Origin of Species"
bibliography: references.bib
---

The origin of species is explained by @Darwin1859; see also @Weiß2015.
Citezot finds the citations in the text. Code chunks are ignored, as are Quarto cross-references such as @fig-map:

qmd <- tempfile(fileext = ".qmd")
writeLines(c(
  "---",
  "bibliography: references.bib",
  "---",
  "The origin of species is explained by @Darwin1859; see also @Weiß2015 and @fig-map.",
  "",
  "```{r}",
  "x@slot  # not a citation",
  "```"
), qmd)

cz_qmd_keys(qmd)
#> [1] "Darwin1859" "Weiß2015"

Now write the bibliography:

cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd")
#> ✔ 2/2 cited keys found; 'references.bib' updated.

and render the document with Quarto as normal (quarto render manuscript.qmd, to HTML, PDF or Typst). Only the cited items are written, in key order, as BibLaTeX straight from Zotero’s exporter. For CSL-YAML give a .yaml name: cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd", out = "references.yaml").

When a key is missing
Suppose the text cites @Kent2002 but the item has no such citekey in Zotero. The update stops and does not touch your existing file:

cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd")
#> Error in `cz_update_bib()`:
#> ! Cited in the documents but not found in Zotero: "Kent2002".
#> ✖ 'references.bib' was NOT touched, because an incomplete bibliography would
#>   break the render.
#> ℹ Pin the citekey in Zotero (see `cz_pin_key()`), check the spelling, or use
#>   `allow_incomplete = TRUE` to write what was found.

Three things can be wrong, and citezot helps with each.

A typo, or the item is there under another key. Search for it:

cz_find("kent blat")
cz_find(doi = "10.1101/gr.229202")

The item is in Zotero but has no key yet. Pin one. Like every write, it is a dry run until you say so:

cz_pin_key("10.1101/gr.229202", "Kent2002")                  # preview
cz_pin_key("10.1101/gr.229202", "Kent2002", dry_run = FALSE) # write

The item is not in your library. Add it from its DOI:

cz_add("10.1101/gr.229202", key = "Kent2002")                  # preview
cz_add("10.1101/gr.229202", key = "Kent2002", dry_run = FALSE) # create

The preview shows the title, authors, date and key it would create, and cz_add() first checks that the DOI and the key are not already in your library. (Only DOIs registered with Crossref are supported so far.)

Run cz_update_bib() again and the document is complete.

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
Fixing an entry
A date is wrong. Preview the change, then apply it:

cz_update_item("Regnier2024", list(date = "in press"))
#> ℹ Dry run: nothing written. Use `dry_run = FALSE` to apply to item ABCD2345 (...).
#> • date: "2026" -> "in press"

cz_update_item("Regnier2024", list(date = "in press"), dry_run = FALSE)

Only fields that change are sent, together with the item’s version. If someone (or Zotero desktop) edited the item after citezot read it, Zotero answers HTTP 412 and nothing is overwritten; run the command again after looking at the item with cz_get_item("Regnier2024"). Creators, tags and collections are replaced as a whole, so to add one tag pass the full list of tags. Identity fields (key, version, itemType, dates added/modified) and the citekey cannot be changed here; use cz_pin_key() for the key.

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
Citekeys
If you use Better BibTeX, your keys follow a pattern such as auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower. citezot can generate keys for new items with the same pattern:

item <- list(
  itemType = "journalArticle",
  title = "On the origin of species by means of natural selection",
  date = "1859",
  creators = list(list(creatorType = "author", firstName = "Charles", lastName = "Darwin"))
)

cz_suggest_key(item, "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower")
#> [1] "darwin1859origin"

# a taken key gets a letter
cz_suggest_key(item, "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower",
               existing = "darwin1859origin")
#> [1] "darwin1859origina"

# Better BibTeX's own default pattern
cz_suggest_key(item, "auth.lower + shorttitle(3,3) + year")
#> [1] "darwinOriginSpeciesMeans1859"

cz_add(..., key = "auto") uses the pattern from cz_key_format(): the citezot.key_format option if you set it, otherwise the one Better BibTeX saved in your Zotero profile, otherwise Better BibTeX’s default. Only a subset of the formula language is supported (auth, year, shorttitle, title, a few filters, +); anything else is an error rather than a different key. Better BibTeX itself is not needed: any key you pin with cz_pin_key() or give to cz_add() works.
Words in titles follow Better BibTeX’s rules: HTML tags are dropped, titles are cut at the first colon or sentence end, short function words such as “a” and “the” are skipped, and hyphens and other punctuation are removed inside words (early-diverging becomes earlydiverging).

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
Speed
A first download of a big library takes tens of seconds. Turn on the cache and later runs only fetch what changed:

options(citezot.cache = TRUE)   # put this in your .Rprofile
system.time(cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd"))
#>    user  system elapsed
#>   0.121   0.019   0.342

The cache lives in tools::R_user_dir("citezot", "cache") and holds bibliographic metadata only. cz_fetch_items(refresh = TRUE) forces a full download, and cz_clear_cache() deletes it.

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
Automating it
Update the bibliography every time the project renders by adding a pre-render step to _quarto.yml:
project:
  pre-render: Rscript -e 'citezot::cz_update_bib()'
In a targets pipeline, return the path and let targets track the file:

tar_target(
  references,
  cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd", quiet = TRUE),
  format = "file",
  cue = tar_cue(mode = "always")
)

Because cz_update_bib() leaves the file alone when nothing changed, the render is only repeated when your references really changed.

title: Writing a manuscript with citezot
text:
Troubleshooting

“Zotero credentials not found.” The environment variables are not set in this R session. Check Sys.getenv("ZOTERO_API_KEY") != "" and restart R after editing ~/.Renviron.
HTTP 403. The key is invalid or lacks the access needed. Writing needs a key with write access.
HTTP 412 on an update. The item changed since it was read. Look at it again with cz_get_item() and retry on purpose.
A cited key “not found” although the item is in Zotero. The item has no citekey saved on it (or a different one). Use cz_find() to see what the item’s key is, and cz_pin_key() to set it.
A key containing odd characters (such as ??) cannot be cited from a document. Fix it in Zotero or with cz_pin_key(..., overwrite = TRUE).

title: citezot
text:
Source code
Report a bug




MIT



Joel H. Nitta
Author, maintainer
The goal of citezot is to make it easy to cite references in Quarto or R Markdown documents using Zotero.
To use citezot, cite sources in your text as usual following Quarto (Pandoc) syntax. For example, manuscript.qmd might contain:
Both references should be in your Zotero library, with the citekeys Darwin1859 and Kenrick1997a saved for those items.
Calling cz_update_bib() generates the references.bib file containing only the references you cited, straight from Zotero:
citezot can also look items up, add them from a DOI, and fix fields, always showing you what it is about to do first.
citezot talks to the Zotero web API, so it works without Zotero desktop running. This means you can use it, e.g., on a server, or to cite references in an automated document generated by GitHub Actions (automated CVs!).
citezot is not affiliated with or endorsed by Zotero.

title: citezot
text:
Installation
citezot is not on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub:
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("joelnitta/citezot")

title: citezot
text:
Setup
You need a Zotero API key and your user ID (kept in ~/.Renviron), and each item you cite needs a citekey. A read-only key is enough for everything except adding and editing items.
See the setup guide for step-by-step instructions.

title: citezot
text:
Usage

Bibliography generation
cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd") # writes the file named by `bibliography:`
cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd", out = "references.yaml") # CSL-YAML instead of BibLaTeX

The output file defaults to the bibliography: of the document’s YAML front matter (or _quarto.yml), else references.bib. BibLaTeX is the default because it works with every Quarto output format, including Typst.
Files that mention sources informally (e.g. a CSV note saying “defined in Darwin1859”) can be scanned too: cz_update_bib(qmd, bare = "data.csv").



It will not quietly lose references
If a key you cited in the document is not in Zotero, cz_update_bib() stops and leaves the existing file untouched, because a bibliography that silently loses entries breaks the render. It will let you know the missing keys and what to do about them. (allow_incomplete = TRUE writes what was found anyway).


Fast enough to run on every render
Fetching a large library takes a while the first time (about 20 s for ~6,000 items, requested in parallel). With caching on, later runs download only what changed: about 0.3 s when nothing did.
# You can put this in your in .Rprofile
# The cache is stored in tools::R_user_dir("citezot", "cache")
options(citezot.cache = TRUE)
Caching is off unless you ask for it. The cache holds bibliographic metadata, never your key; cz_clear_cache() deletes it.

title: citezot
text:
Finding, adding and fixing items
Everything that changes your library is a dry run unless you say otherwise: it reads, shows exactly what would happen, and writes nothing until you add dry_run = FALSE. There is no delete.
cz_find("darwin origin of species") # free text
#>       item           citekey author year
#> 1 MEIQ8FY5        Darwin1859 Darwin 1859
#> 2 MY4FLB35 katz2018extending   Katz 2018
#>                                                                                                                                   title
#> 1                On the origin of species by means of natural selection, or the preservation of favoured races in the struggle for life
#> 2 Extending the scope of Darwin’s ‘abominable mystery’: integrative approaches to understanding angiosperm origins and species richness
#>         doi            type
#> 1      <NA>            book
#> 2 10/gb4dc5 article-journal
cz_find(doi = "10.2307/1796430") # by DOI, ISBN or exact citekey
#>       item       citekey             author year
#> 1 JVIYHN3W MacArthur1967 MacArthur & Wilson 1967
#>                               title             doi type
#> 1 The theory of island biogeography 10.2307/1796430 book
cz_find(citekey = "Darwin1859")
#>       item    citekey author year
#> 1 MEIQ8FY5 Darwin1859 Darwin 1859
#>                                                                                                                    title
#> 1 On the origin of species by means of natural selection, or the preservation of favoured races in the struggle for life
#>    doi type
#> 1 <NA> book

cz_add("10.1016/0022-5193(64)90038-4", key = "auto")
#> ℹ Citekey formula `auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower` read from your
#>   Zotero profile (Better BibTeX).
#> ℹ Dry run: nothing written. Use `dry_run = FALSE` to add this item.
#> • type: journalArticle
#> • title: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I
#> • authors: Hamilton W.D.
#> • date: 1964-07
#> • in: Journal of Theoretical Biology
#> • DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(64)90038-4
#> • citekey: hamilton1964genetical
#> This message is displayed once per session.

cz_update_item("Darwin1859", list(publisher = "John Murray"))
#> ℹ Dry run: nothing written. Use `dry_run = FALSE` to apply to item MEIQ8FY5 (On
#>   the origin of species by means of natural sele…).
#> • publisher: "J Murray" -> "John Murray"
Wherever a function takes an item, you can give a DOI, a Zotero item ID, an existing citekey, or a one-row result of cz_find().

cz_add() looks the DOI up in Crossref, checks the item is not already in your library (and that the citekey is unused and valid for pandoc), builds the item from Zotero’s own template for its type, and pins the key in the same request. Each request carries a write token, so a retry after a network error cannot create the item twice. Only Crossref DOIs are supported so far.
cz_update_item() sends only the fields that actually change, together with the item version. If the item was edited elsewhere in the meantime, Zotero refuses (HTTP 412) and nothing is overwritten. Creators, tags and collections are replaced as a whole, as Zotero does.
cz_pin_key() refuses to replace a different pinned key unless you pass overwrite = TRUE, since that would break documents that cite the old one.


Generating citekeys
key = "auto" builds the key from a Better BibTeX-style formula, such as auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower (giving hamilton1964genetical).
The key formula comes from, in order: options(citezot.key_format = "..."); the pattern saved in your Zotero profile by Better BibTeX (citezot reads that one setting from Zotero’s prefs.js, only when it generates a key, and tells you once per session); or Better BibTeX’s default pattern. If the same key already exists, a letter is appended to the new one (a, b, …).
Only a documented subset of the formula language is supported; anything else is an error rather than a different key. Check what is in use with cz_key_format() and try a formula with cz_suggest_key().
item <- list(
  itemType = "journalArticle",
  title = "The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I",
  date = "1964-07",
  creators = list(list(
    creatorType = "author",
    firstName = "W. D.",
    lastName = "Hamilton"
  ))
)
cz_suggest_key(item, "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower")
#> [1] "hamilton1964genetical"
cz_suggest_key(
  item,
  "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower",
  existing = "hamilton1964genetical"
)
#> [1] "hamilton1964geneticala"

title: citezot
text:
Automation
Instead of manually running cz_update_bib(), you may want to automatically run it every time your document is rendered.
A Quarto pre-render step in _quarto.yml will do this:
project:
  pre-render: Rscript -e 'citezot::cz_update_bib()'
If you use targets, you could specify a target that is re-checked on every tar_make():
tar_target(
  references,
  cz_update_bib("manuscript.qmd", quiet = TRUE),
  format = "file",
  cue = tar_cue(mode = "always")
)

title: citezot
section: How it differs from other packages
text:
How it differs from other packages
rbbt is built around RStudio, particularly its add-in for inserting citations while you write. It needs Zotero desktop running with the Better BibTeX plugin.
zot is a general-purpose Zotero client. It works at a lower (more direct) level, with versioned writes, batch plans, file attachments and read-only queries of the local database.
c2z imports references into Zotero from many sources (including DOIs, ISBNs and the Norwegian Cristin registry), and can edit, copy and delete items.
citezot seeks to be lightweight (minimal package dependencies), to make bibliography maintenance simple (one function call builds your bibliography), to be careful with your library (every write is a dry run unless you say otherwise, and nothing can be deleted), and to work across platforms, even without Zotero running.
These descriptions are based on each package’s documentation, not its code. Please check their pages for the current state.

title: citezot
text:
Limitations

Item lookup by identifier supports Crossref DOIs only (ISBN, arXiv and PMID are planned).
Nothing can be deleted through citezot.
BibLaTeX output comes from Zotero’s own exporter, and CSL-YAML from the library’s CSL-JSON, so what you see in Quarto is what Zotero’s exporters produce.
Matching is by the citekey stored on the item; items without one cannot be cited.

title: citezot
text:
Development
To work on citezot, clone the repository and install its development dependencies (pak::local_install_dev_deps()). The checks that run before each commit use pre-commit; install it once (for example brew install pre-commit or pip install pre-commit), then enable the hooks in your clone:
pre-commit install

Before every commit, the hooks run styler and lintr (tidyverse style, 80 columns; see .lintr) and check that README.md has been rendered from README.Rmd. Run them by hand with pre-commit run --all-files.
Before every push, a hook runs devtools::check() and refuses the push unless it has no errors, warnings or notes.
The tests make no network calls (devtools::test()). Edit README.Rmd, not README.md, and render it with devtools::build_readme(). Some of its examples read from a Zotero library, so rendering needs Zotero credentials (see the setup guide) and the items cited in the examples; if you cannot render it, say so in your pull request.

title: citezot
text:
Getting help
Documentation, including a worked example, is at https://joelnitta.github.io/citezot/ (or the manuscript guide once installed). Please report bugs and ideas at https://github.com/joelnitta/citezot/issues.

title: citezot
text:
License
citezot is released under the MIT license.

title: Setting up citezot
text:
This is the one-time setup. It takes about five minutes, and you do not need to repeat it for each project. You need to:
None of the code in this guide is run when the site is built, because it needs your Zotero account.

title: Setting up citezot
text:
1. Create an API key
citezot talks to the Zotero web API, so it needs an API key. Zotero desktop does not have to be running, but your library must be synced to zotero.org (in Zotero desktop: Settings, Sync).


Sign in at https://www.zotero.org/settings/keys and choose Create new private key.
Give it a name you will recognise, such as citezot (read only).
Under Personal library, tick Allow library access and leave Allow write access unticked. This is enough for cz_update_bib(), cz_find(), cz_get_item() and cz_fetch_items().
Save the key and copy it now. Zotero shows the key only once.
Note your numeric user ID. It is shown on the same page, in the sentence “Your userID for use in API calls is …”. It is not your user name.


Two keys are better than one
The functions that change your library (cz_add(), cz_update_item() and cz_pin_key()) need a key with Allow write access. Rather than giving that power to every session, create a second key, citezot (write), and use it only when you are adding or editing items. Everything that writes is a dry run unless you pass dry_run = FALSE, and citezot has no delete, but a key that cannot write is the strongest guarantee.


Group libraries
For a group library, create the key under Group permissions on the same page. The group ID is the number in the group’s URL (https://www.zotero.org/groups/<ID>/<name>). Then use cz_auth(library_type = "group").

title: Setting up citezot
text:
2. Tell R about the key
citezot reads these environment variables:







Variable
What it holds




ZOTERO_API_KEY
the API key


ZOTERO_USER_ID
the numeric ID of your personal library


ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID
optional; used in preference to ZOTERO_USER_ID, and the only name used for group libraries



Put them in your user-level .Renviron, so they are available in every project and cannot be committed by accident:

usethis::edit_r_environ()   # opens ~/.Renviron

ZOTERO_API_KEY=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
ZOTERO_USER_ID=1234567
Save the file and restart R: .Renviron is read only at startup. Then check that citezot can see the credentials. The key is never printed:

library(citezot)
cz_auth()
#> <cz_auth> user library 1234567 (API key hidden)

If you switch between a read-only and a write key, use cz_auth(api_key = "...") for the session that needs the other one, or keep the write key in a second variable and pass it explicitly, for example cz_auth(api_key = Sys.getenv("ZOTERO_WRITE_KEY")), then give that object to the auth argument of the function.
Do not put the key in a file inside a project. If you must, make sure the file is in .gitignore.

What citezot does with your key

It sends the key only to api.zotero.org, as a bearer token.
It never prints, logs or stores it. print() on an auth object hides it.
The optional cache (see cz_clear_cache()) holds bibliographic metadata, never the key.

title: Setting up citezot
section: 3. Make sure your items have citekeys
text:
3. Make sure your items have citekeys
citezot cites an item by the citekey saved on it. An item without one cannot be cited, and cz_update_bib() will tell you which keys it could not find.
There are two ways to get a key onto an item.

With Better BibTeX (recommended if you already use it)
Better BibTeX generates keys from a formula you choose, and can pin them so they never change. Pinned keys are saved on the item, which is what citezot reads. In Zotero desktop, select the items, right-click, then Better BibTeX and Pin BibTeX key. Syncing then uploads the keys.
Better BibTeX is optional. citezot does not need it to read keys.


Without Better BibTeX
Zotero stores the key in each item’s Citation Key field. You can set it by hand in Zotero, or from R:

cz_find("darwin origin of species")             # find the item
cz_pin_key("Darwin1859", "Darwin1859")          # preview; item = any of the identifiers cz_find() understands
cz_add("10.1016/0022-5193(64)90038-4", key = "auto")        # or add a new item with a generated key

See the manuscript guide for the full workflow, including how new keys are generated.

title: Setting up citezot
text:
Troubleshooting

“Zotero credentials not found.” The variables are not set in this R session. Check Sys.getenv("ZOTERO_API_KEY") != "", and restart R after editing .Renviron.
HTTP 403. The key is invalid, or lacks the access you asked for (for example, a read-only key used to add an item).
HTTP 404 for a library that exists. The user ID is wrong. Use the number, not the user name.
Items you just added in Zotero desktop are missing. The library has not synced yet.

title: Zotero credentials
text:
Description
Resolves the library ID and API key, by default from the environment variables ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID (or, for a user library, ZOTERO_USER_ID) and ZOTERO_API_KEY. Load them yourself (e.g. from a gitignored .Renviron or .env.local); citezot never reads files or stores the key. The key is never printed.

title: Zotero credentials
text:
Usage
cz_auth(
  library_id = NULL,
  api_key = Sys.getenv("ZOTERO_API_KEY"),
  library_type = c("user", "group")
)

title: Zotero credentials
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




library_id
Numeric user ID (or group ID), as a string or number. If NULL (default), taken from ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID; for a user library ZOTERO_USER_ID is used as a fallback.


api_key
Zotero API key.


library_type
"user" (personal library) or "group".

title: Zotero credentials
text:
Details
Create a key at https://www.zotero.org/settings/keys; the numeric user ID is on the same page. A read-only key is enough for cz_fetch_items(); use a separate key with write access for functions that change the library.

title: Zotero credentials
text:
Value
A cz_auth object, for the auth argument of other functions.

title: Zotero credentials
text:
Examples

# Explicit values (normally these come from environment variables). The key
# is never shown when the object is printed.
cz_auth(library_id = "1234567", api_key = "not-a-real-key")

<cz_auth> user library 1234567 (API key hidden)

title: Find items in your Zotero library
text: cz_find

title: Find items in your Zotero library
text:
Description
Searches the library for items matching all the criteria given. Matching is done locally on the library’s CSL-JSON (see cz_fetch_items()), because Zotero’s server-side search cannot look items up by DOI or citekey. Use cache = TRUE (or options(citezot.cache = TRUE)) to make this fast on repeat calls.

title: Find items in your Zotero library
text:
Usage
cz_find(
  query = NULL,
  doi = NULL,
  isbn = NULL,
  citekey = NULL,
  auth = cz_auth(),
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE),
  items = NULL
)

title: Find items in your Zotero library
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




query
Free text. Every word must appear (case-insensitively) in the title, authors, year, journal or citekey.


doi
A DOI, with or without a https://doi.org/ or doi: prefix.


isbn
An ISBN (hyphens and spaces are ignored).


citekey
An exact pinned citekey.


auth
Credentials from cz_auth().


cache
Passed to cz_fetch_items().


items
Items already fetched with cz_fetch_items(), to avoid fetching again.

title: Find items in your Zotero library
text:
Value
A data frame with one row per match and columns item (Zotero item ID), citekey, author, year, title, doi and type. It can be passed as the item argument of cz_pin_key() when it has one row.

title: Find items in your Zotero library
text:
Examples
cz_find(doi = "10.3767/000651906X622210")
cz_find("Ebihara Hymenophyllaceae revision")
cz_find(citekey = "Ebihara2006")

title: Get a CSL item’s pinned citekey, however it is pinned

Arguments

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text: R/write.R

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text: cz_pin_key

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text:
Description
Sets the item’s native citationKey field via the Web API (the same field a desktop Better BibTeX install manages), so cz_item_key() and cz_fetch_items() see it. Requires a key with write access.

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text:
Usage
cz_pin_key(
  item,
  key,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  auth = cz_auth(),
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE)
)

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




item
The item to pin: a DOI, a Zotero item ID (bare, "Q62TD7I9", or with the library ID as in CSL-JSON, "6265773/Q62TD7I9"), an existing citekey, or a one-row result of cz_find(). Zero or several matches is an error.


key
The citekey to pin.


dry_run
If TRUE (default), report what would change and write nothing.


overwrite
Replace a different key that is already pinned. Defaults to FALSE, because changing a pinned key breaks documents citing it.


auth
Credentials from cz_auth().


cache
Passed to cz_fetch_items() when item is a DOI or citekey that has to be looked up.

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text:
Details
The default is a dry run: the item is read (to get its current version and key) but nothing is written. Set dry_run = FALSE to write. The write sends If-Unmodified-Since-Version, so if the item changed in the meantime Zotero rejects it (HTTP 412) and nothing is overwritten.

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
text:
Value
Invisibly, a list with item, before, after and written.

title: Pin a citekey onto a Zotero item
Suggest a citekey for an item
text: R/key-format.R

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text: cz_suggest_key

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text:
Description
Builds a key from a Better BibTeX-style formula, e.g. "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower". If the key is already taken, a letter (a, b, …) is appended, as Better BibTeX does.

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text:
Usage
cz_suggest_key(item, formula = NULL, existing = character())

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




item
A Zotero native item (as from cz_get_item(), or the payload cz_add() builds) or a CSL-JSON item.


formula
The key formula. See Details.


existing
Keys already in use, so the result can be made unique.

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text:
Details
The formula is, in order of preference, the formula argument, then the one found by cz_key_format() (the citezot.key_format option, your Zotero profile’s Better BibTeX pattern, or Better BibTeX’s default auth.lower + shorttitle(3,3) + year). Supported functions are auth (first author’s last name), year, shorttitle(n, m) (first n words of the title, skipping short function words, with the first m capitalised), and title; filters are lower, upper, fold, transliterate, clean, condense and nopunct; terms are joined with + and quoted text is kept as is. Anything else is an error rather than a silently different key. The result is ASCII and safe to cite in pandoc.

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text:
Value
A single string.

title: Suggest a citekey for an item
text:
Examples

item <- list(
  itemType = "journalArticle",
  title = "A taxonomic revision of Hymenophyllaceae",
  date = "2006",
  creators = list(list(creatorType = "author", firstName = "A", lastName = "Ebihara"))
)
cz_suggest_key(item, "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower")

[1] "ebihara2006taxonomic"

cz_suggest_key(item, existing = "ebihara2006taxonomic",
               formula = "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1).lower")

[1] "ebihara2006taxonomica"

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text: R/item.R

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text: cz_update_item

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text:
Description
Changes selected fields of one item and shows exactly what will change. The default is a dry run: the item is read and a before/after diff is shown, but nothing is written. Use dry_run = FALSE to write.

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text:
Usage
cz_update_item(
  item,
  fields,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  auth = cz_auth(),
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE)
)

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text:
Arguments







Arguments
Description




item
The item: a DOI, Zotero item ID, citekey, or one-row result of cz_find().


fields
A named list of new values, e.g. list(date = "in press", DOI = "10.1234/abc"). Names must be fields that exist for the item’s type; see names(cz_get_item(item)$data).


dry_run
If TRUE (default), show the diff and write nothing.


auth
Credentials from cz_auth() (a key with write access to write).


cache
Passed to cz_fetch_items() when item has to be looked up.

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text:
Details
Only fields whose value actually changes are sent (a PATCH), together with If-Unmodified-Since-Version: if the item was edited elsewhere since it was read, Zotero rejects the write (HTTP 412) and nothing is overwritten.
Plain fields take a single string (use "" to clear one). creators, tags, collections and relations take lists and are replaced as a whole, so to add one tag pass the full list of tags. Identity and bookkeeping fields (key, version, itemType, dates, parentItem, deleted) can’t be changed, and the citekey is changed with cz_pin_key().

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text:
Value
Invisibly, a list with item, changes (for each changed field, its before and after) and written.

title: Update fields of a Zotero item
text:
Examples
cz_update_item("Regnier2024", list(date = "in press"))                  # preview
cz_update_item("Regnier2024", list(date = "in press"), dry_run = FALSE) # write
